Task Guide: Task: Generate a symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB) in an aluminum system using LAMMPS. The simulation should use metal units, and define a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice structure with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Define a three-dimensional simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. Create two atomic regions: an upper region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 1], y: [0 -1 3], z: [1 0 0]) and a lower region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 -1], y: [0 1 3], z: [1 0 0]). Populate these regions with atoms according to their respective orientations to form a Σ5(310) symmetric tilt grain boundary. To remove unrealistic atomic overlaps, displace one region if necessary and delete overlapping atoms when the nearest neighbour distance is below a threshold of 0.35 Å. Compute relevant atomic properties, including centrosymmetry and per-atom potential energy, to assess the structural quality of the generated grain boundary. Perform an initial energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with energy and force tolerances of 1e-15 and a maximum of 5000 iterations. Save the minimized configuration in a dump file. Conduct a second energy minimization while allowing the simulation box to relax in the direction perpendicular to the grain boundary to ensure an energetically stable configuration. Save the final minimized structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS data format. Calculate the grain boundary energy using a reference bulk energy per atom of −3.360000 eV. Compute the total system energy, subtract the bulk energy contribution, and normalize by the grain boundary area. Convert the result to mJ/m² and round the final value. As the final output, return the computed grain boundary energy in mJ/m². Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_10/task_10_trial_2 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

# LAMMPS Input Script for Generating a Symmetric Tilt Grain Boundary in Aluminum

units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p

# Define the FCC lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å
lattice fcc 4.05

# Create a simulation box
region whole block 0 10 0 10 0 10 units lattice
create_box 1 whole

# Define the potential
pair_style eam
pair_coeff * * /potentials/EAM/Al99.eam.alloy Al

# Define the upper region with a specific orientation
region upper block 0 10 5 10 0 10 units lattice
create_atoms 1 region upper
orient x 0 3 1
orient y 0 -1 3
orient z 1 0 0

# Define the lower region with a specific orientation
region lower block 0 10 0 5 0 10 units lattice
create_atoms 1 region lower
orient x 0 3 -1
orient y 0 1 3
orient z 1 0 0

# Remove overlapping atoms
delete_atoms overlap 0.35 all all

# Compute properties
compute csym all centro/atom
compute pe all pe/atom

# Initial energy minimization
min_style cg
minimize 1e-15 1e-15 5000 10000

dump 1 all custom 100 /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_10/task_10_trial_2/dump.minimized id type x y z c_csym c_pe

# Second energy minimization with box relaxation
fix 1 all box/relax aniso 0.0 vmax 0.001
minimize 1e-15 1e-15 5000 10000

# Save the final minimized structure
write_data /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_10/task_10_trial_2/final_structure.data

# Calculate grain boundary energy
variable bulk_energy equal -3.360000
variable total_energy equal pe
variable gb_area equal "lx*ly"
variable gb_energy equal "(v_total_energy - count(all)*v_bulk_energy)/v_gb_area*16021.76565"
print "Grain boundary energy: ${gb_energy} mJ/m^2"
"}
